name: ASCII / Dither Resolve
summary: Everything starts as a coarse field of characters and sharpens into crisp UI as Acme Pulse understands it, except the one coral cluster that refuses to resolve.
look: Ink glyphs (. : - = + * # @) on near-white paper render every image as brightness. A resolution HUD and a teal seam turn the noisy field into clean white cards; the anomaly stays as hot coral characters until a decision card rises out of it.

components.name: Character-ramp field
components.role: mono glyph grid that renders any image as brightness; the not-yet-understood state

components.name: Resolution HUD
components.role: 'RES 32 → 4 px' readout that shows progress without a progress bar

components.name: Resolve seam
components.role: teal vertical wipe with glow; ASCII on one side, clean UI on the other

components.name: Hot glyph cluster
components.role: coral #@# characters that refuse to resolve; the anomaly

components.name: Resolved pills
components.role: crisp white metric rows with green ticks; what healthy looks like

components.name: Decision card
components.role: coral-ringed card rising from the hot cluster with Roll back / Acknowledge

motion.name: Resolution pull
motion.how: cell size 32→4 px in steps(6), one step per beat at 120 BPM (0.5 s)

motion.name: Glyph scramble
motion.how: each character cycles the ramp before landing, 60 ms/char, 8 ms seeded stagger

motion.name: Seam wipe
motion.how: vertical mask left→right, expo.inOut 0.6 s, triggered on the 0:08 drop

story: Hook: a wall of dashboards exists only as scrambling ASCII while the panel asks 'How many dashboards did you check today?'. Reveal: on the drop a teal seam wipes the noise away, leaving the Acme mark and 'Acme Pulse' on clean paper. Proof: the checkout-conversion chart is still glyphs; four healthy metrics resolve into pills, the drop stays coral and a card rises: 'Checkout conversion −18% · since 09:42 · after deploy #2231' with Roll back. CTA: glyphs retreat to the edges; 'Every metric. Every minute.' and Start free resolve crisp.
adapt: Render a screenshot of your own UI through the character ramp, resolve it section by section, and leave your product's key finding as the last hot cluster.

fit.risk: Dense glyph fields turn to moiré under video compression; keep hero cells at 8 px or more.
